extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/Principal Investigators applying for ERC Synergy Grants (and their institutional research support offices)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how ERC Synergy Grant proposals are evaluated across stages, the sole evaluation criterion (scientific excellence with outstanding synergetic effect), required team composition, and scoring. Useful for applicants preparing B1/B2 and interview materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sole evaluation criterion — Scientific excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated on the sole criterion of scientific excellence, which takes on the additional meaning of "outstanding intrinsic synergetic effect."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All assessments (project and PIs) must be framed against scientific excellence; for Synergy Grants this explicitly includes an expectation of an outstanding intrinsic synergetic effect among team members and elements of the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synergy
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers assess 'Synergy' as a distinct feature when assessing the excellence of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The team must demonstrate that the science is genuinely synergistic — not just collaborative. Synergy should be evident in the project design, combined approaches, and expected emergent outcomes that could not be achieved by individual PIs working separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complementarity of the Principal Investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers assess the 'Complementarity of the Principal Investigators' as a distinct feature when assessing the excellence of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers look for complementary expertise and track records among the PIs that together enable the proposed ambitious research. CVs and track records (provided in B1) are used to judge complementarity and capability to deliver the synergistic agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative working arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers assess 'Collaborative working arrangements' as a distinct feature when assessing the excellence of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should describe how the PIs will work together (management, responsibilities, interactions). The practicality and suitability of the collaborative arrangements are evaluated, including evidence that the planned interactions will realize the claimed synergy. These arrangements should also be clearly conveyed during the interview presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers assess 'Risk' as a distinct feature when assessing the excellence of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider the level and nature of scientific/technical risk in the proposal as part of the excellence assessment. Proposals should address and justify risks inherent in ambitious, synergistic research and explain mitigation or rationale for accepting high-risk approaches where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 evaluation — B1 content
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 1: Only part B1 is evaluated (5-page project summary, CVs, track records).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At Stage 1 reviewers focus exclusively on the concise project summary and PI CVs/track records. B1 must succinctly present the project's ambition, synergy rationale, and evidence of PI complementarity and capability because progression to Stage 2 depends on the B1 assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 evaluation — full proposal (B1 + B2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 2: The entire proposal is evaluated, i.e., B1 and B2 (15-page project description). The complete proposal is reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At Stage 2 reviewers assess the full project description (B2) in combination with B1, allowing detailed evaluation of methodology, work plans, justification of synergy, and the collaborative arrangements described in the longer narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 3 evaluation — interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 3: The interview is the final stage of the evaluation. The aspects demonstrated in the presentation should clearly convey the synergistic nature of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must use the interview to demonstrate and clarify the synergistic aspects of the project, how PIs will interact, and to answer questions about risks and feasibility. Presentation should make the intrinsic synergy evident to the panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal scoring — A/B/C grading
rubrics_metrics.description: The evaluation of the Principal Investigators and the project is carried out with a grading: A/B/C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both individual PIs and the project are graded using the A/B/C scale. (The page lists the grading system but does not define the detailed meaning of each grade — applicants should assume this grading is applied to judge excellence and suitability for funding.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel composition — multidisciplinary fit
rubrics_metrics.description: To account for complex interdisciplinary projects, the panels' composition is dynamic and subject to change in order to fit the multidisciplinary nature of the proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The evaluation panels will be organized/adjusted to ensure suitable expertise covers the proposal's multidisciplinary aspects. Applicants should expect panels tailored to the proposal's disciplinary mix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group composition — number and joint ambition of PIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Synergy Grants support 2-4 Principal Investigators (Corresponding PI + 1-3 PIs) who jointly address ambitious research problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams must consist of 2–4 PIs and collectively demonstrate the ambition and genuine synergy required by the scheme. The proposal should explain why the chosen number and combination of PIs is necessary to achieve the proposed outcomes.
